waterbody.name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River
waterbody.locality: Puerto Princesa City, Palawan; exact sampling stations are not named in the abstract
waterbody.kind: subterranean river/cave with marine-estuarine and limited freshwater influence

question: Does the 2025 WPU RIDE conference abstract provide enough station-resolved, reusable freshwater and estuarine fish evidence for Bangwit's Palawan coverage?

source.title: Beyond the Wonders: Unraveling the Aquatic Faunal Diversity of Puerto Princesa Subterranean River, Palawan, Philippines
source.provider: Western Philippines University, Department of Research, Innovation, Development, and Extension (RIDE)
source.citation: Balisco, R. A. T., Huang, W.-C., Jhuang, W.-C., Shalah, B., & Liao, T.-Y. (2025). Beyond the Wonders: Unraveling the Aquatic Faunal Diversity of Puerto Princesa Subterranean River, Palawan, Philippines. WPU RIDE Annual Conference 2025 Book of Abstracts, p. 87.

reportedStudy.collectionMethodSummary: Various baited traps; water depth and surface salinity were recorded at each sampling station.
reportedStudy.freshwaterContext: The abstract says most species are euryhaline and only a few primary freshwater species were encountered; it does not name those species or give their station assignments.

comparisonWithEarlierAbstract.interpretation: The later abstract does not state whether its two-season set is independent of, expands, or reanalyzes the 2023 preliminary survey. The totals cannot be treated as a measured increase or as 18 additional species.

limits: The conference abstract is not a full methods paper or a species-by-station/season table; it gives no fish names, voucher/accession identifiers, DNA sequence links, exact collection dates, station count, or station coordinates.
The 4.2 km figure describes the cave labyrinth explored, not a validated distribution polygon or complete river survey footprint.
The label 'subterranean river' does not establish that all sampled sites are freshwater. The abstract describes mostly euryhaline taxa and only a few unnamed primary freshwater species.
The 2023 preliminary abstract reported 13 total species from a four-day survey; the 2025 abstract does not establish whether the work overlaps its two-season counts.
The book carries a 2025 WPU RIDE copyright notice; no item-specific license or permission for reuse of a derived public species list was established.
No protected-area access, fishing rules, catchability, natural diet, safety status, or current-presence claim was reviewed.

followUp.nextAction: Look for an openly accessible full report or supplement that names taxa by station and season and states sampling dates, vouchers or sequence identifiers, and reuse terms. If none is available, continue Palawan freshwater-source discovery rather than infer species from the aggregate abstract.
